content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To know why religion was so controversial, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Read primary sources on the Edict of Nantes (4 hours)
Step 2. Analyze the impact of the Council of Trent (3 days)
Step 3. Draft a summary of the Great Schism (2 hours)
Step 4. Review the life of Thomas Aquinas (5 hours)
Step 5. Research the origins of the Protestant Reformation (1 week)
Step 6. Map the spread of Islam in the 7th century (6 hours)
Step 7. Write a comparative essay on religious wars (2 days)
Step 8. Evaluate the role of the Printing Press in dissent (1 day)
Step 9. Examine the relationship between Church and State in the Middle Ages (3 days)
Step 10. Catalog the theological disputes of the 4th century (4 days)
Step 11. Study the influence of the Roman Empire on early Christianity (10 days)
Step 12. Interview a historian specializing in the Inquisition (2 hours)
Step 13. Compare the Huguenot movement to the Catholic League (1 day)
Step 14. Watch a documentary on the Thirty Years' War (3 hours)
Step 15. Outline the core tenets of the Counter-Reformation (5 hours)
Step 16. Research the Enlightenment's critique of organized religion (1 week)
Step 17. Visit a local theological library (4 hours)
Step 18. Buy a textbook on World Religions (30 minutes)
Step 19. Investigate the Investiture Controversy (2 days)
Step 20. Read about the First Council of Nicaea (6 hours)
Step 21. Listen to a podcast on the Crusades (1 hour)
Step 22. Examine the Gregorian Reforms (3 days)
Step 23. Study the impact of the Peace of Westphalia (12 hours)
Step 24. Look into the trials of Galileo Galilei (1 day)
Step 25. Research the influence of the Byzantine Empire (4 days)
Step 26. Analyze the role of religious iconography (5 hours)
Step 27. Summarize the effects of the French Revolution on the Church (8 hours)
Step 28. Take an online course on the Reformation (2 weeks)
Step 29. Write a report on secularization trends (3 days)
Step 30. Select a list of influential religious leaders (1 hour)
Step 31. Survey the history of religious pluralism (1 week)
Step 32. Read Martin Luther’s 95 Theses (2 hours)
Step 33. Collect art from the Renaissance period (4 hours)
Step 34. Consult with a religious studies professor (1 hour)
Step 35. Browse the university bookstore for philosophy titles (45 minutes)
Step 36. Document the rise of mysticism in the 14th century (6 hours)
Step 37. Identify the major schisms in the early church (2 days)
Step 38. Study the writings of John Calvin (1 week)
Step 39. Map the route of the Third Crusade (3 hours)
Step 40. Research the impact of the Scientific Revolution (5 days)
Step 41. Attend a seminar on religious sociology (3 hours)
Step 42. Read the Declaration of the Rights of Man (1 hour)
Step 43. Compile all notes into a final thesis (4 days)
Step 44. Review the Napoleonic Concordat (4 hours)
Step 45. Present findings to a peer review group (2 hours)
Step 46. Register for a history symposium (15 minutes)
Step 47. Examine the role of the Papacy in European politics (4 days)
Step 48. Explore the intersection of faith and science (2 days)
Step 49. Create a timeline of religious conflicts (5 hours)
Step 50. Analyze the demographic shifts following the Black Death (3 days)
